body:
WHAT
If the workspace has a `STANDARDS.md` at its root (or `.magentra/STANDARDS.md` as a fallback), its contents are added to the system prompt under a header saying they are binding rules that win over default code-style guidance. The file is read again on every system-prompt build, so edits apply on the next request without a restart. Content larger than 16 KB is cut at the last line boundary and a truncation notice is appended.

WHY
Project rules must reach the model every turn and follow live edits; an unbounded file would silently eat the context window.

WHERE
engine/core/src/knowledge/standards.ts — STANDARDS_FILENAMES, MAX_STANDARDS_BYTES = 16384, TRUNCATION_NOTICE, loadStandards(cwd). Consumed by engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.buildSystemPrompt() (`const standards = loadStandards(this.cwd)` on each build; STANDARDS_SECTION_HEADER prompt id system.standards-header; Session.section()) and the wrap-up nudge `mentionStandards`.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With a STANDARDS.md containing 'RULE-XYZ', the FakeProvider request's system prompt contains '# Coding standards (user-provided — binding)' followed by 'RULE-XYZ'.
2. With no STANDARDS.md (and no .magentra/STANDARDS.md), loadStandards returns undefined and the system prompt has no standards header.
3. Editing STANDARDS.md between two turns (no /clear) changes the second request's system prompt to the new content.
4. A 20 KB STANDARDS.md yields text whose UTF-8 byte length is at most 16384 plus the notice, ends with '[standards truncated at 16KB — condense the file]', and cuts at a newline boundary.
5. A whitespace-only root STANDARDS.md is skipped and the .magentra/STANDARDS.md fallback is used when present.
